Monotonicity yields the inequality with the correct sign. The zero-translation case and arbitrary real R are handled without circular reliance.

Normalization gives the pointwise averaged-difference identity. Product integrability follows from domination by ρ on a finite-measure ball, justifying Fubini. Kernel support permits each translation estimate, and C ≥ 0 justifies the final bound. A separate ε > 0 assumption is unnecessary: normalization and support already force it.

The proof supplies the exact common real bound L = max(1, 2Lρ·volume(tsupport ρ)). Change of variables and domination by two translated support indicators yield the global Lipschitz estimate uniformly in F. Compactness and measurability justify every integral.
